name: Iraqi narrator (approved default)

request_body_template.text: <SCRIPT — Iraqi dialect; spell Iraqi qaf as گ, e.g. ضيگ، صدگني، بوكت>
request_body_template.instructions: You are a mature Iraqi man from Baghdad in his late forties, a professional documentary narrator, speaking in your own natural Baghdadi Iraqi dialect — not Modern Standard Arabic, not Gulf, Egyptian or Levantine. The letter گ is the Iraqi hard G (ضيگ = ḍīg, صدگني = ṣaddigni). بوكت = b-wakit, إحنا = iḥna, شنو = shinu. Voice: low, warm, deep and clear; calm and confident. Emotion is sincere and understated, like a quiet word to a friend — never acting, no exaggerated sadness, no big pitch swings. Natural fluent Iraqi conversational pace, the way a Baghdadi actually talks: not slow, not rushed. The whole read must fit in <TARGET_SECONDS minus ~2> seconds. Keep pauses short and natural: a light breath between sentences, a brief beat at commas. Sentence endings fall softly.

take_selection: The engine varies between takes. Render 2–4 takes and keep the one closest to the reference: median pitch about 100 Hz, pitch spread about 4–4.5 semitones, every word correct in speech recognition, qaf heard as g.
post_production: Shorten pauses only (about 0.4 s between sentences, about 0.3 s at commas); keep breaths; no time-stretch or pitch shift
Resample 24 kHz to 48 kHz (soxr), 65 Hz high-pass, 11.5 kHz low-pass, 2:1 compression (threshold -22 dB)
Target -16 LUFS integrated, true peak at or below -2 dBTP, no clipping
Deliver audio only (MP3 320 kb/s + WAV 48 kHz/24-bit) unless the user asks for video
